biography.plain_text: Guo Wengui, also known as Miles Kwok, is a Chinese businessman who built his fortune in property development. His Beijing interests included Pangu Plaza, combining offices and a hotel near the Olympic Stadium. He also held an indirect stake in the brokerage Founder Securities and has lived in the United States.

long_biography.plain_text:
Property developer Guo Wengui entered real estate through a furniture enterprise in Zhengzhou. Expanding into construction required more capital than the manufacturer could provide alone. He formed Yuda Real Estate with Hong Kong investor Ailian in 1993, initially pursuing modest commercial and residential buildings before the company undertook the Yuda International Trade Center.

For his later Pangu development in Beijing, architect C. Y. Lee's team arranged five buildings into a dragon-shaped composition. Completed in 2008 beside the Olympic precinct, the project combined different uses within a single architectural scheme. Its long connecting corridor and Chinese cultural references were part of the architects' stated design approach.
